authored_by: build session (Opus), by hand, before any digest was generated
conclusions: PostgreSQL was chosen as the primary database for the new project.
The choice was made on PostgreSQL's JSONB support and the team's existing familiarity with it.
That PostgreSQL was already running in the existing stack weighed heavily in the recommendation, because switching would mean rebuilding connections, migrations, ORM layer and healthchecks.
CockroachDB was rejected: it only wins when multi-region active-active replication is a hard requirement, and it adds operational overhead and cost on a single-VPS deployment.
MySQL was rejected: it would add a second relational engine with no unique advantage over PostgreSQL for this stack.
Left open: which task to start with (schema initialisation, JSONB indexing strategy, connection pooling, backups, or migrations tooling) was asked and never answered.
